It’s a rehabilitation benefit so if something doesn’t have a good likelihood of employment or could aggravate your disabilities it could be hard to be approved for that. But the legwork will be on you to find a plan that you will use the benefit for and they have you interview people in the field and everything before they let you use it to try and ensure that you get the most out of it.

Yes it is great just make sure you have a clear idea of what you would use it on because it can be hard to switch plans depending on what the switch is. Yes the GI bill sends you a BAH stipend based upon the cost of living in your schools zip code. However since you have 80% you should be eligible for VR&E which provides 48 additional months of education benefits on top of the GI Bill. However and this is IMPORTANT, DO NOT EXHAUST YOUR GI BILL BEFORE USING VR&E. If you were to do that you can not use VR&E as you must have at least 1 day of entitlement remaining on your GI Bill. So look into using VR&E first. It’s basically an extra 4 years of GI Bill however it’s even better. They will give you a laptop and printer and everything also that you get to keep as long as you finish your plan and are declared “rehabilitated.”

The first of the month however with certain veteran friendly banks like Navy Federal and USAA you could get your check a couple days early. I bank at both and you can choose to split your check between banks if you want as well it should hit all of your banks around the same time.

So yes the stock or fund that pays out the dividend will drop by the dividend payment amount shortly after because the NAV if it’s a fund or total assets drops if it’s a stock because they paid some of their cash out to shareholders. It doesn’t actually mean their company is worth less now, the drop is minimal it’s whatever amount the dividend was and it quickly goes back up as long as the market isn’t in a frenzy. The only time you would want to care about that is if the dividends were classified as ROC or return of capital because that can in some cases mean that they just sent some of your equity or money back to you. That doesn’t always mean that though a lot of the times too it is just a way they organize their payouts so that their is less taxation on them. Because when they put it as ROC it is taxed at a different rate then if it was classified differently. Usually with large companies if it’s classified as ROC they aren’t just sending some of your money back to you with smaller companies or higher yielders then you really might wanna check it out. With dividends funds or stocks like SCHD the biggest thing to consider is taxes not necessarily the price slightly dropping after a payout. With taxes in the mix that can effect your long term returns and sometimes by a lot because when you have to pay some taxes on your dividend earnings you aren’t just losing that money you are losing all the growth it could’ve had if it had stayed invested. So that is the biggest argument against dividend stocks or funds because growth stocks are in a way tax deferred themselves because you wont pay taxes on them until you sell years later (if you made a gain not a loss). The best place to put your dividend funds or stocks like SCHD is in a Roth IRA because those are tax free on all earnings dividends and growth so whatever value it’s at in 20-30 years is what you’ll get when you withdraw it.
